title: Introduction to complement and its complex nomenclature
why: The lecturer introduces the topic, acknowledges its complex nomenclature, and frames the session's scope.

title: Overview of complement activation and effector functions
why: The lecturer outlines the three stages of complement and summarizes its main immunological and janitorial functions.

title: Complement numbering and cleavage fragment nomenclature
why: The lecturer explains the historical numbering system, cleavage fragment labels, and exceptions within complement naming.

title: C3 activation, C3b surface binding and C3a inflammation
why: The lecturer details the cleavage of C3 into C3a and C3b and the reactive thioester bond mechanism that drives covalent binding.

title: Three complement activation pathways and their timing
why: The lecturer describes how spontaneous tick-over creates fluid-phase convertases that deposit C3b onto pathogen surfaces to amplify convertase generation.

title: Alternative pathway initiation and surface amplification
why: It details the step-by-step mechanism of the alternative pathway from fluid-phase convertase formation to surface amplification.

title: Lectin pathway recognition and C3 convertase formation
why: The lecturer explains how mannose-binding lectin recognizes bacterial sugars to assemble the classical convertase and deposit C3b.

title: Classical pathway activation and the local complement threshold
why: The lecturer explains antibody-mediated activation via C1 and how local concentration of convertases overcomes clearance mechanisms to reach a trigger threshold.

title: Complement-mediated opsonization and phagocytosis
why: The lecturer explains the three downstream effector actions of activated complement, including phagocytic signaling, generic inflammation, and MAC pore formation.

title: C3a-mediated inflammation and cell recruitment
why: The lecturer explains how C3a acts as a soluble inflammatory mediator to recruit immune cells to the infection site.

title: Membrane attack complex assembly and pathogen lysis
why: The lecturer details the mechanism of C5 convertase, pore formation by C5b through C9, and why the membrane attack complex targets certain pathogens but not others.

title: Complement regulation and protection of host cells
why: The lecturer details the regulatory proteins that protect host cells by inhibiting convertases and blocking membrane attack complex insertion.

title: Clinical consequences of complement component deficiencies
why: The lecturer systematically reviews how genetic and secondary deficiencies in distinct complement proteins produce specific clinical outcomes.

title: Pathogen complement evasion and applications of staphylococcal protein A
why: The lecturer describes strategies pathogens use to avoid complement destruction, focusing on Staphylococcus aureus adaptations and the practical uses of protein A.

title: Lecture close: Transition to adaptive immunity
why: The lecturer delivers concluding remarks and states the topic of the upcoming lecture.
